question: True or false: on early silent-era film stock, red lips photographed almost black?
answer: True. Orthochromatic stock responded to blue and green light but hardly at all to red, so red came out dark and blue skies bleached to white. Make-up was designed around it, with pale bases and lip colours chosen for how they read in grey. Panchromatic stock, sensitive to red, took over in the later 1920s.
move: A recording shows what the instrument could sense, not what was there.
ask: Which picture of reality do I hold that only shows what my instrument could sense?
trap: Assuming film sees each colour as bright as the eye does.
reference: Salt, Film Style and Technology: History and Analysis, 2nd edn, Starword, 1992
